meta: Dramas like My ID Is Gangnam Beauty: campus romance that treats appearance as a system, not a makeover montage.
standfirst: A 7.6 aggregate from 102,026 ratings against a written-review average of 8.83 is the tell, and both numbers are defensible. It is a campus romance where the surgery is the premise rather than the payoff, and it is also a very common first Korean drama, which flatters it in memory and rarely survives a rewatch. The male lead is played so still that whether it reads as restraint or as blankness is a coin toss, his early treatment of her looks worse the second time, and the themes it raises about appearance are dropped before they are finished.

picks.why: The closest thing in the catalog, and it is about the same wound. A young woman whose body is public property, a first love with somebody who already knew her, and a campus that keeps ranking people. Both refuse to make the transformation the point, and both are funniest when the friend group takes over. Difference: it is far warmer and comfort 5 against comfort 4, with no bullying flashbacks, so the ache here is nostalgic rather than raw.

The same university, read as a threat. Webtoon source, Korean campus hierarchy, group projects as power plays, and a male lead whose kindness is a question rather than a fact. Both shows understand that most of the cruelty at that age is procedural. Difference: it is a psychological study with no comfort in it, and the adaptation abandons its own ending, so do not come here for the resolution this one gives you.

Youth written by somebody who remembers it hurting. Same interest in a young woman deciding what she is worth outside other people's assessment, same slow-burn first love, same friend group doing the heavy lifting. Difference: it is framed by an adult looking back, and the frame is sad on purpose, so the ending recolours everything in front of it.

A school story about being cast in somebody else's plot. Both take a girl who has been assigned a role by everybody around her and let her fight the assignment, and both are webtoon adaptations that use a high school as a machine for ranking people. Difference: the fantasy premise takes over completely, so the social realism that makes Gangnam Beauty sting is replaced by rules and twists.

The adult version of the same quiet. Two people who communicate carefully, a university and a sports world that both punish anyone who steps out of line, and a romance built from consideration rather than tension. Difference: the pace is genuinely slow and there is no bullying plot or comic ensemble, so it asks more patience and gives less relief.

Youth, difference, and a kid learning what his parents survived. Same tenderness toward a teenager who has been treated as a problem, same use of a school as the arena. Difference: it is a time-travel fantasy with a music-club heart, so the social critique is replaced by sentiment, and it is aimed younger.

against.title: True Beauty
against.why: The obvious pick, and it is the opposite film with the same logline. The makeover works, the secret is a farce engine, and the show is never interested in why anyone needed it. Gangnam Beauty puts the surgery in episode one precisely so it cannot be the ending.

against.title: Boys Over Flowers
against.why: Still the default campus recommendation, and it will read as a period piece. The hierarchy is a fantasy about wealth rather than a study of appearance, and the male lead's cruelty is styled as romance. That is the exact convention this show was written against.

against.title: Love Alarm
against.why: Paired for the school setting and the webtoon origin, and the reason it fails is that it has no interest in its own premise. An app that reveals attraction is a great idea used for a love triangle and then dropped. The social machinery here is the subject, not the gimmick.
